_comment: Copy this to your PROJECT's .omp/team.config.json (fallback: .claude/team.config.json for legacy projects) and adjust. These values ARE the built-in defaults — the interpreter behaves identically when the file is absent. Per-project config exists so role→agent/scope resolution is deterministic and explicit instead of inferred at runtime.
_custom_agents: roles values are passed verbatim to Task `agent`. Use the registered bare name of a project (.omp/agents/), user (~/.omp/agent/agents/), or enabled extension-package agent; the OMP agent registry is flat. Examples: 'backend' could map to 'my-go-backend', and 'security-tester' to 'pentester'.
_roster_overrides_example: Add/replace agents on a stage without editing workflows/*.json. Applied after the profile's conditional[] rules. Uncomment and adapt:
_scope_map_order: Evaluated TOP-TO-BOTTOM, FIRST matching glob wins. Order specific paths above generic extensions. `mobile` MUST stay above `backend-kotlin`: a KMP source file (e.g. shared/src/commonMain/Foo.kt) matches both **/commonMain/** (mobile) and **/*.kt (backend-kotlin) — mobile wins only because it is listed first. So **/*.kt routes to backend-kotlin only when NOT under a mobile source set (e.g. a Spring src/main/kotlin).
_has_ui_note: There is deliberately NO flags.has_ui / flags.has_runtime here. Both are interpreter built-ins: has_ui = (scope ∩ {frontend, mobile} ≠ ∅); has_runtime = the task touches any executable/deployable code scope (false only for docs/config-only). has_runtime GATES the manual_qa stage (so backend/CLI runtime checks run too); has_ui SELECTS the mode within it (ui vs runtime). A project MAY override via flags.has_ui / flags.has_runtime (schema allows it via additionalProperties), but that creates a second source of truth — prefer the built-ins.
